title: Module 14 quiz — Security, HA and DR
description: Eight questions on TLS/PKI, IAM/secrets, encryption, DNS/LB, 99.99% failure domains, RTO/RPO, HA capacity. Synthetic BayPay.

questions.prompt: Merchants fail HTTPS to payments.apps.baypay.example while a jump box can GET :8080 on a RUNNING task. What have you proven so far?
choices: Postgres is down
Edge TLS (or DNS to the edge) is in the suspect set; the process may still be healthy
The Kubernetes tls Secret from Module 10 is the only possible cause
You should disable TLS to restore payments
questions.explanation: HTTP-healthy tasks plus merchant handshake failure is a symptom class. Quote the cert/ACM/DNS files before you name a cause.

questions.prompt: Which IAM split is required for a Fargate payment task?
choices: One AdministratorAccess role for everything
Execution role pulls image/secrets; task role is the app’s AWS API identity — neither is AdministratorAccess
The DMGR identity is reused
Access keys committed in task-def JSON

questions.prompt: Where may BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD live in production?
choices: Git next to the Terraform root
A KMS-backed secret store (or equivalent), never in git or a dashboard JSON
A Micrometer label named password
The leftover PaymentCluster custom service as the long-term home
questions.explanation: Encryption at rest of the secret + TLS in transit. No changeme.

questions.prompt: A 99.99% design for payment create is roughly how much unavailability per year, and what is not automatic?
choices: 52 seconds; you must add a second region
About 52 minutes; multi-region is a DR choice, not a free upgrade from multi-AZ
Zero minutes; 99.99% means never fail
43 minutes; that is the Module 13 99.9% monthly budget reused as yearly
questions.explanation: ARCHITECT-1401: single-region multi-AZ can be a 99.99% design. DR-1403 is the region-loss tabletop.

questions.prompt: What is RPO versus RTO for a us-west-2 regional outage?
choices: RPO is how fast DNS flips; RTO is the TLS expiry window
RPO is how much payment intent you can lose; RTO is how long until you take new POSTs again
They are the same number as the 99.9% error budget
RPO is the number of AZs; RTO is the number of tasks
questions.explanation: L-14.6 / DR-1403. Payments vs reporting may have different pairs.

questions.prompt: Which leftover object is not a DR target when us-west-2 is gone?
choices: Encrypted payment backups and the idempotency store
BayPayCell / dmgr-east / PaymentCluster
A paper warm standby in us-east-1
Route 53 failover records you designed on paper
questions.explanation: Traditional ND is the source estate. Do not fail over to the cell.

questions.prompt: Module 14 capacity planning is mainly which question?
choices: What P99 is on a single happy-path POST in H2
How much unused N+1 / failover / DR capacity you pay for so a domain can die
Whether to set -Xmx equal to the task memory limit
How many NAT Gateways a 90-minute lab should apply
questions.explanation: L-14.7 is HA/DR headroom. L-13.5 is SLO-driven pool/RPS headroom.

questions.prompt: A threat model for POST /api/v1/payments must include which item?
choices: A working exploit payload against a live bank
Idempotency-Key replay, frozen-account bypass, and secret leakage — as STRIDE notes, not as attack scripts
A new WebSphere cell in Docker
AdministratorAccess as the recommended task role
questions.explanation: SECURITY-1404 is architecture notes. No exploit PoCs.
